original_question: For each integer t, does there exist a threshold Delta_t such that every graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) > Delta_t satisfies omega(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t? If such a threshold exists, can the same conclusion be strengthened from the clique number of G^2 to the coloring, list-coloring, painting, or Alon-Tarsi parameters of G^2, namely chi(G^2), chi_l(G^2), chi_p(G^2), or chi_AT(G^2)?
target_in_paper: Question 4 in Section 2 ("Graphs in General: Wegner's Conjecture"), restated as item 2 in Section 6 ("Open Problems and Conjectures").
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's exact target. It correctly quantifies over each integer t, asks for a large-maximum-degree threshold Delta_t, uses the bound omega(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, and then asks whether the same deficit can be forced for the square's chromatic, list-chromatic, paint, and Alon-Tarsi numbers. It also correctly treats the problem as one about general graphs, not a planar or sparse subclass.
missing_details: The paper states the hypothesis as Delta(G) >= Delta_t, not Delta(G) > Delta_t.
To make the question fully stand-alone, define the square G^2 as the graph on V(G) in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when their distance in G is at most 2.
Clarify the notation used in the paper: chi^2(G)=chi(G^2), chi^2_l(G)=chi_l(G^2), chi^2_p(G)=chi_p(G^2), and chi^2_AT(G)=chi_AT(G^2).
State explicitly that Delta(G) is the maximum degree of G and omega(G^2) is the clique number of G^2.
The paper assumes standard finite simple graph terminology; Question 4 itself imposes no extra assumptions such as connectedness, planarity, girth, bounded mad, or minor exclusions.

The paper phrases the strengthening as four specific progressively stronger candidate conclusions: (i) chi(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, (ii) chi_l(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, (iii) chi_p(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, and even (iv) chi_AT(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t.
refined_question: For each integer t, does there exist a constant Delta_t such that every finite simple graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) >= Delta_t satisfies omega(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, where G^2 is the graph on V(G) in which two vertices are adjacent whenever their distance in G is at most 2? Moreover, can this conclusion be strengthened to any of the following bounds on the square of G: chi(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, chi_l(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, chi_p(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, or even chi_AT(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Question 4, which your draft matches almost verbatim. The introduction supplies the needed notation for graph squares and the parameters chi, chi_l, chi_p, and chi_AT. The local context also shows why this is the right target: Lemma 1 gives the basic t=1 clique deficit omega(G^2) <= Delta^2 - 1 when G^2 is not the Moore-graph clique, and Theorem 2 strengthens that t=1 statement to the Alon-Tarsi parameter for connected graphs outside the exceptional Moore-graph cases. Question 4 then asks whether one can force an arbitrary fixed deficit t below Delta^2 for sufficiently large maximum degree, first for omega(G^2) and then for the stronger parameters chi(G^2), chi_l(G^2), chi_p(G^2), and chi_AT(G^2). Section 6 confirms this identification by restating the same problem as open problem 2.
